The All-China Labour Federation to the All-India
Trade Union Congress.

Dear Comrades!

The All-China Labour Federation sends comradely fraternal
greetings to the toiling masses of India and wishes the Ninth
All-India Trade Union Congress success. We wish your Congress
the greatest success in its endeavour to express and define
a revolutionary programme of action and to rally the rebellious
working class and peasant masses for the struggles against
exploitation and oppression.
The All-China Labour Federation is well aware of the
enormous difficulties which are confronting your struggles
for higher wages, shorter work-day etc. We are well aware,
likewise, of the trials you must undergo in the course of
your arduous fight to overthrow foreign domination, to crush
the rule of British imperialism, and to attain complete
national independence and the liberation of the Indian working
masses from Subjugation and humiliation. All this we comprehend
fully, because we are in the very midst of such a struggle.
The Chinese working class and peasant masses are fighting a
life-and-death struggle against the combind counter-revolutionary
forces - the imperialists and the Kuomintang. The masses under
the leadership of the All-China Labour Federation are deter-
mined to drive out from China the British, Japanese, American
and French imperialists, and to overthrow the Kuomintang and
the Nanking Government, the running dogs of the imperialists
and the traitors to the Chinese revolution. Thus notwithstanding
the raging white terror of the Kuomintang, the systematic and
most ruthless mass executions and massacres of revolutionary
workers and peasants, strikes and political mass demonstrations
of ever-increasing dimensions are frequently taking place.
Last but not least, the mass uprisings of the peasants are
spreading all over the country and large sections of Southern
China are already governed by the Soviets, established and
controlled by the local revolutionary workers, peasants
and Red Army soldiers.
Of course, not only our own and your struggles but also
the revolutionary movements of all other colonial and semi-
colonial peoples, and that of the workers and peasants in parti-
cular, will be greatly accelerated as soon as a revolutionary
united mass front of all the oppressed and exploited against
the capitalists and landlords, the militarists and imperialists
as well against working class traitors will be set up and
co-ordinated. The oppressed and exploited masses of all
countries, nationalities and races must realise once and for
all that a united front with, or the leadership of such people
as the MacDonalds, Purcells, Citrines, Bunji Suzukis, Chiang
Kai-Sheks, Nehrus etc. inevitably lead the workers' and pea-
sants' movements to the most crushing defeats. It is therefore,
essential to expose before the masses the treacherous policies
and activities of these people and eliminate them without fail
from our class organisations. Unless such traitors are dis-
carded and their reformist policies repudiated national inde-
pendence in India or elsewhere is not attainable and the eman-
cipation of the working class and peasant masses is impossible.
Hence with profound appreciation we learned the fact that
the restless and rebellious masses of your country are in deep
sympathy with Soviet Russia and its aspirations; that your
Trade Union Congress took steps in the promotion of a revo-
lutionary united front and trade union unity on the Pacific
by selecting delegates to attend the Pan-Pacific Trade Union

中华全国总工会致全印度工会大会。

亲爱的同志们！

中华全国总工会向印度的劳苦大众致以同志般的兄弟问候，并祝愿第九次全印度工会大会取得成功。我们祝愿贵大会在努力表达和制定革命行动纲领、团结反抗的工人阶级和农民群众进行反剥削反压迫斗争方面取得最大成功。
中华全国总工会充分意识到你们在争取提高工资、缩短工作日等斗争中所面临的巨大困难。我们也同样清楚，你们在推翻外国统治、粉碎英国帝国主义统治、实现完全民族独立以及将印度劳动大众从被征服和屈辱中解放出来的艰苦斗争过程中必须经受的考验。对此我们完全理解，因为我们正身处这样的斗争之中。中国工人阶级和农民群众正在与联合的反革命势力——帝国主义者和国民党——进行生死斗争。在中华全国总工会领导下的群众决心将英国、日本、美国和法国帝国主义者赶出中国，并推翻作为帝国主义走狗和中国革命叛徒的国民党及南京政府。因此，尽管国民党实行猖獗的白色恐怖，对革命工人和农民进行系统且最残忍的大规模处决和屠杀，但规模日益扩大的罢工和政治性群众示威仍频繁发生。最后但同样重要的是，农民的大规模起义正在全国各地蔓延，中国南方的大片地区已由当地革命工人、农民和红军士兵建立并控制的苏维埃政权治理。
当然，不仅是我们自身和你们的斗争，而且所有其他殖民地和半殖民地人民的革命运动，特别是工人和农民的革命运动，一旦建立起并协调好所有受压迫和被剥削者反对资本家、地主、军阀和帝国主义以及反对工人阶级叛徒的革命统一战线，都将大大加速。各国、各民族和各阶层的受压迫和被剥削群众必须一劳永逸地认识到，与麦克唐纳（MacDonalds）、珀塞尔斯（Purcells）、西特林斯（Citrines）、铃木文治（Bunji Suzukis）、蒋介石、尼赫鲁（Nehrus）等人结成统一战线或接受其领导，必然导致工人和农民运动遭受最惨重的失败。因此，必须在群众面前揭露这些人的背叛政策和活动，并务必将他们从我们的阶级组织中清除出去。除非抛弃此类叛徒并摒弃其改良主义政策，否则印度或其他地方的民族独立无法实现，工人阶级和农民大众的解放也不可能实现。因此，我们怀着深深的赞赏获悉，贵国不安分且充满反抗精神的群众对苏维埃俄国及其愿望深表同情；获悉贵工会大会采取了促进太平洋地区革命统一战线和工会统一的步骤，选派代表参加了去年在我国举行的泛太平洋工会

Conference in our country last year, and that it had condemned
the British government in refusing passports to the delegates.
The All-China Labour Federation followed with the greatest
sympathy the determined fight of the Bombay Textile Workers
in their strike, the brave struggles of the Railway and the
Steel Workers; the boycott of the Simon Commission as well as the
militant action taken by your delegates at the so-called "Com-
monwealth Labour Conference" at London and the Brussels
Congress of the Second International. We rejoiced at their
walking out of these social-imperialists gatherings which not
only called upon the workers to pursue the so-called industrial
peace policy"Mondism" but even went on record in opposition
to national independence for India and other colonies, as well
as most viciously attacking Soviet Russia, the only real friend
of the colonial peoples and the stronghold of the world prole-
tariat. Obviously the words uttered by your delegate, Chaman
Lall, that"the British Labour Party, together with the Second
International, are the advance guard of British and European
imperialism in order to prevent and postpone the emancipation
of the colonial Peoples" are strikingly true and marvelous
words which your Congress and all of us should take due notice of.
However, at the same time we learn with regret that many
of your Trade Union Congress leaders have joined hands with
the treacherous leaders of the British Labour Party, the
General Council of the British Trade Union Congress, the Second
International and its tail-end the Amsterdam International
(International Federation of Trade Unions with headquarters
at Amsterdam). Indeed we were astonished to read in your
official publication the urging by Mr. N.M. Joshi, General
Secretary of your Trade Union Congress to the effect that
the All-India Trade Union Congress should join the Amsterdam
International, the systematic splitter of the world trade union
movement and the most persistent saboteur of all efforts by
the Trade Unions of Soviet Russia and the Red International
of Labour Unions (with headquarters at Moscow) to bring about
trade union unity the world over. We read with deep disgust
your secretary's call to join and strengthen the Amsterdam
International, the most cunning disrupter of mass strikes,
liberation movement uprisings and the upholder of the counter
revolution in China. Not less outrageous and treacherous is
the proposal of Mr.Joshi that the All-India Trade Union Con-
gress in co-operation with Bunji Suzuki, Matsuoka, Yonekubu
& Co., the Japanese champions of the Amsterdam International
and the bought agents of Japanese imperialism should through
the so-called Geneva Labour Office convene an "Asiatic Labour
Conference" thus purposely ignoring and undermining the
Pan-Pacific Trade Union Secretariat, established at the Pan-
Pacific Trade Union Conference last year as previously referred
to, and composed of the Trade Unions of Soviet Russia, Australia,
Indonesia, China, the Philippines, Korea, and the Left Wing
Trade Unions of Japan, England, France, America and Canada.
Yes, consciously and deliberately, Joshi, Bunji Suzuki & Co,
are striving to disrupt the Pan-Pacific Trade Union Congress
to be convened by the Pan-Pacific Trade Union Secretariat
in the summer of 1929.
Evidently Mr. Joshi and his like are preparing to betray
your Trade Union Congress as Mr. Nehru and his like did it
recently in your national independence movement or, as was
the case with the Chiang Kai-Sheks in our country last year.
The betrayal in our country took place as soon as the workers
and peasants became class conscious and were fighting not only
the foreign invader imperialists but the native exploiters as
well. In other words, as soon as the Chinese revolutionary masses
established the eight hour day, confiscated and redistributed the
land, set up the workers' and Peasants' government, etc., the
bourgeoisie, feudalists, militarists, social-reformists and weak

会议，并谴责英国政府拒绝向代表发放护照的行为。
中华全国总工会以最同情的态度关注了孟买纺织工人在罢工中的坚定斗争、铁路工人和钢铁工人的英勇斗争、抵制西蒙委员会（Simon Commission）的行动，以及贵方代表在伦敦所谓的“英联邦劳工会议”和第二国际布鲁塞尔大会上采取的激进行动。我们为他们退出这些社会帝国主义者的集会而感到高兴，这些集会不仅号召工人推行所谓的“工业和平政策”即“蒙德主义”（Mondism），甚至记录在案反对印度及其他殖民地的民族独立，并对苏维埃俄国——殖民地人民唯一真正的朋友和世界无产阶级的堡垒——进行了最恶毒的攻击。显然，贵方代表查曼·拉尔（Chaman Lall）所说的“英国工党连同第二国际是英国和欧洲帝国主义的前卫队，旨在阻止和推迟殖民地人民的解放”这句话是惊人真实且精辟的言论，贵大会和我们大家都应予以充分重视。
然而，与此同时，我们遗憾地获悉，贵工会大会的许多领导人已与英国工党、英国工会大会总理事会、第二国际及其附庸阿姆斯特丹国际（总部设在阿姆斯特丹的国际工会联合会）的背叛性领导人勾结在一起。的确，当我们读到贵方官方出版物中刊登的贵工会大会总书记 N.M. 乔希（N.M. Joshi）先生的呼吁时感到震惊，他主张全印度工会大会加入阿姆斯特丹国际，而该组织是世界工会运动的系统性分裂者，也是破坏苏维埃俄国工会和红色工会国际（总部设在莫斯科）为实现全球工会统一所作一切努力的最顽固的破坏者。我们怀着深深的厌恶读到了贵方书记关于加入并加强阿姆斯特丹国际的呼吁，该国际是大规模罢工、解放运动起义的最狡猾的破坏者，也是中国反革命的维护者。乔希先生提议全印度工会大会与铃木文治、松冈、米仓（Yonekubu）等人合作，召开一次所谓的“亚洲劳工会议”，这一提议同样令人愤慨和背叛，因为这些人是日本帝国主义收买的代理人，也是阿姆斯特丹国际在日本的拥护者，此举故意无视并削弱去年在泛太平洋工会会议上建立的泛太平洋工会秘书处，该秘书处由苏维埃俄国、澳大利亚、印度尼西亚、中国、菲律宾、朝鲜的工会以及日本、英国、法国、美国和加拿大的左翼工会组成。是的，乔希、铃木文治等人正有意识且蓄意地试图破坏由泛太平洋工会秘书处计划于1929年夏季召开的泛太平洋工会大会。
显然，乔希先生之流正准备像尼赫鲁先生之流最近在贵国民族独立运动中所做的那样，或者像去年我国蒋介石之流所做的那样，背叛贵工会大会。我国的背叛发生在工人和农民阶级意识觉醒并开始不仅反抗外国入侵的帝国主义者，而且反抗本国剥削者之时。换言之，一旦中国革命群众确立了八小时工作制，没收并重新分配土地，建立工农政府等，资产阶级、封建主义者、军阀、社会改良主义者以及各种软弱的

kneel leaders of every description deserted the revolution and
went over to the camp of the counter revolution and white
terror. We presume that your revolutionary movement is rapidly
approaching a somewhat similar stage of development.
The All-China Labour Federation hopes that the All-India
Trade Union Congress in session, and the local unions, or the
rank and file in particular, will not follow the footsteps of
Joshi & Co., but will formulate and promulgate fighting policies,
and grasp out out-stretched hand for a revolutionary united
mass front under the leadership of the Pan-Pacific Trade
Union Secretariat. We sincerely hope that your Congress will
not endorse social-imperialism nor join the Amsterdam Inter-
national and thus permit the Joshis to throw the weight of
your trade unions on the side of the bourgeoisie and its running
dogs, the reformists and traitors. On the contrary, we hope
that your trade unions will rather strengthen their connections
and bonds with the trade unions of Soviet Russia and the Far-
East, and that we will meet your representatives at the coming
Pan-Pacific Trade Union Congress. We urge and call upon you
to join hands with us in order to fight more effectively imperi-
alism and the threatening imperialist war, to defend jointly
Soviet Russia and with an increasing energy to foster the fight
for the liberation of the oppressed colonial peoples and victory
for the working class.
In conclusion the All-China Labour Federation extends to
your Trade Union Congress a cordial invitation to pay a visit
to our country and to be an eye witness to the brutal massacres
of our comrades by the Kuomintang, the component part and friend
of the Amsterdam and Second Internationals; to learn from the
most authentic source the character and driving forces of the
great Chinese revolution as well as to exchange with us views
and revolutionary experiences.
Down With Imperialism and Its Running Dogs!
Long Live the Revolutionary United Mass Front of
All Oppressed and Exploited.
All-China Labour Federation,
Son-Chao-Jen, Chairman,
Lou-Tan-hsian, Secretary,
Shanghai, October 10, 1928.

膝软领袖便背离革命，投奔反革命和白色恐怖的阵营。我们推测，贵国的革命运动正迅速接近类似的发展阶段。
中华全国总工会希望正在开会的全印度工会大会、各地方工会，特别是基层会员，不要步乔希之流的后尘，而是制定并颁布战斗政策，抓住我们伸出的手，在泛太平洋工会秘书处的领导下建立革命统一战线。我们真诚希望贵大会不要认可社会帝国主义，也不要加入阿姆斯特丹国际，从而让乔希之流将贵工会的力量投向资产阶级及其走狗、改良主义者和叛徒一边。相反，我们希望贵工会加强与苏维埃俄国及远东地区工会的联系和纽带，并期待在即将召开的泛太平洋工会大会上会见贵方代表。我们敦促并呼吁你们与我们携手，更有效地打击帝国主义和迫在眉睫的帝国主义战争，共同保卫苏维埃俄国，并以日益增强的精力促进受压迫殖民地人民的解放斗争和无产阶级的胜利。
最后，中华全国总工会向贵工会大会发出诚挚邀请，请莅临我国，亲眼目睹作为阿姆斯特丹国际和第二国际组成部分及朋友的国民党对我们同志进行的残酷屠杀；从最可靠的来源了解伟大中国革命的性质和动力，并与我们交流观点和革命经验。
打倒帝国主义及其走狗！
所有受压迫和被剥削者的革命统一战线万岁！
中华全国总工会，
主席：孙兆仁（音译，Son-Chao-Jen），
书记：楼坦贤（音译，Lou-Tan-hsian），
上海，1928年10月10日。

In the imperialist war for the oppression of the colonies, the main tasks of the international proletariat are, a) to propagate in the imperialist armies a defeatist attitude; b) to organise national minority armies and lead them in a revolutionary manner; c) to propagate fraternisation between the soldiers in the imperialist armies and the soldiers in the revolutionary armies in the colonies; d) to turn the war for the suppression of the colonies into civil war; e) to fight against such slogans as the defence of the fatherland, the protection of citizens abroad, and the solution of the problem of over-population; f) to oppose the sending of gun-boats and the transportation of imperialist troops to the colonies, the increasing of the war budget and the extension of the term of military service, etc; g) to send capable Party members to the imperialist armies ████ ████ ██ ████ and navies in the colonies to do organisation and propaganda work, and to send comrades to brother parties in the colonies to help them to do anti-imperialist work in the armies. The work must be connected with the national revolutionary movements in the colonies; h) if there are troops recruited from colonial peoples in the imperialist army such as Indians, Annamites African Negroes, Party members from such colonial countries should be appointed to work among such troops; i) work among the sailors in the navy should be intensified by the different parties. This work will not only help the proletarian revolution in the imperialist countries, but it will be of great importance to the fight against war directed against the Soviet Union and and suppression of colonial revolution; j) to oppose the supply of ammunition, technicians, and advisers to the counter-revolutionary armies in the colonies; k) to oppose the imperialist intervention in the civil wars in the colonies and the granting of loans by the imperialist███████████████████ to the counter-revolutionary governments and militarists in the colonies; l) to fight against the imperialist military preparations in the concessions, railroads, and on the rivers in the colonies; m) to ████ oppose the imperialist butchery in the colonies and all the measures which the imperialists adopt for helping the native counter-revolutionary governments to suppress the masses.

In the war among the imperialists for the exploitation of the colonies, the following methods in addition to the above-mentioned must be used: a) to turn the war among the imperialists for the exploitation of the colonies into a civil war, and to work for the defeat of all the imperialist powers engaged in the war; b) to oppose the assistance of the native militarist groups engaged in a war among themselves by the imperialists; c) to oppose all imperialist militarist preparations in the colonies before the breaking out of the war. Apart from this, application can be made of the general tasks both before and after the breaking out of imperialist wars.

In regard to the preparations for civil war, a new point should be added to the four points suggested in the theses. Military organisation and training occupies an exceptionally important place in the proletarian masses in the colonial countries and countries with a mercenary army. 在帝国主义压迫殖民地的战争中，国际无产阶级的主要任务是：a) 在帝国主义军队中宣传失败主义态度；b) 组织少数民族军队并以革命方式领导他们；c) 宣传帝国主义军队中的士兵与殖民地革命军队中的士兵之间的 fraternisation（联欢/亲善）；d) 将镇压殖民地的战争转变为内战；e) 反对诸如保卫祖国、保护海外公民以及解决人口过剩问题等口号；f) 反对向殖民地派遣炮舰和运输帝国主义军队，反对增加军费预算和延长服役期限等；g) 派遣有能力的党员进入帝国主义在殖民地的陆军 ████ ████ ██ ████ 和海军中进行组织和宣传工作，并派遣同志前往殖民地的兄弟党派，帮助他们在军队中开展反帝工作。这项工作必须与殖民地的民族革命运动相结合；h) 如果帝国主义军队中有从殖民地人民中招募的部队，如印度人、安南人（越南人）、非洲黑人，则应任命来自这些殖民地国家的党员在这些部队中开展工作；i) 各党派应加强在海员中的工作。这项工作不仅有助于帝国主义国家的无产阶级革命，而且对于反对针对苏联的战争以及镇压殖民地革命具有重要意义；j) 反对向殖民地的反革命军队提供弹药、技术人员和顾问；k) 反对帝国主义干涉殖民地的内战，以及帝国主义███████████████████向殖民地的反革命政府和军阀提供贷款；l) 反对帝国主义在殖民地的租界、铁路和河流上的军事准备；m) 反对帝国主义在殖民地的屠杀行为，以及帝国主义为帮助本地反革命政府镇压民众而采取的一切措施。

The Chinese Revolution is a very good example
of national wars. During the Chinese Revolution in
1925-27, the Chinese Communist Party led the Chinese
proletariat to take part in the war for the unification
of Kwangtung and the Northern Expedition, both of which
were carried out under the leadership of the Chinese
bourgeoisie. During both wars, the Chinese Communist
Party made many opportunist errors, in the struggles
against the Rightward movement of the bourgeoisie and
the struggle for leadership of the revolution. These
opportunist mistakes also affected our attitude towards
the national wars. This is because although formally
the war for unification of Kwangtung and the Northern
Expedition are Anti-militarist struggles in fact,
objectively, they are primarily struggles which are
bound to shake the foundation of imperialist rule in
China. Thus with the support and assistance of the
workers in the Hongkong Strike, the war for the unifica-
tion of Kwangtung succeeded in dealing a severe blow
to the British imperialists and forced them to carry
out the 25% surtax proposal. With the support of the
Wuhan workers and the active participation of the
peasants of Hunan and Hupeh, the Northern Expedition
succeeded in taking back the British Concessions in
Hankow and Kiukiang.
Because this civil war was revolutionary, was
led by the proletariat, and participated in by the
peasants, the objective task of the Chinese Communist
Party should have been to establish our own class army,
to extend the workers and peasant military organisations
and training so as to assist the proletariat in its
struggle for the hegemony in the revolution. But the
Chinese Communist Party had practically overlooked
all these points. Although the objective conditions

apparatus to carry out our own work in the army. And
further, the Party never tried to create our own
military force. Our Party had never realised that the
mercenary character of the National Revolutionary Army
was a source of danger and that the whole army could
be easily turned into the tool of the militarists.
Our Party were chiefly engaged in political

中国革命是民族战争的一个很好的例子。在1925-27年的中国革命期间，中国共产党领导中国无产阶级参加了统一广东的战争和北伐战争，这两场战争都是在中国资产阶级的领导下进行的。在这两次战争中，中国共产党在反对资产阶级右倾运动和争取革命领导权的斗争中，犯了许多机会主义错误。这些机会主义错误也影响了我们对民族战争的态度。这是因为，虽然形式上统一广东的战争和北伐战争是反军阀斗争，但实际上，客观上它们主要是必然动摇帝国主义在华统治基础的斗争。因此，在香港罢工工人的支持和协助下，统一广东的战争成功给予英国帝国主义者以沉重打击，迫使他们实施征收25%附加税的方案。在武汉工人的支持和湖南、湖北农民的积极参与下，北伐战争成功收回了汉口和九江的英国租界。

sources of the military defeat of the proletariat in the
Northern Expedition. Thus, when Wuhan followed Nanking
and walked into the counter-revolutionary camp, our Party
could only use the armies of Yeh Ting and Ho Lung to make

defeat, and was not able to go a step forward and con-
vert this protest into civil war for the overthrow of the
political power of the bourgeoisie, the militarists and the
gentry.
    At the beginning we had about 15,000 soldiers in
the armies of Ho Lung and Yeh Ting. We had also soldiers'
nuclei of the Party functioning fairly well and officers
who are Party members. There were also armed workers and
peasants who participated in the uprising. But although
the aim of the Nanchang Uprising was the outcome of the
agrarian revolution, yet it has done practically nothing
to promote the agrarian revolution. During the 50 days
southward march of the revolutionary army from Nanchang
to Swatow, the regions through which we marched were never
touched by the agrarian revolution. Thus this army not
only failed to do positive work as a Workers and Peasants
Army, but it even failed to achieve the results of a
peasant partisan troop.
    The army received correct leadership only after
its defeat, when about over a thousand men of the remnants
of Yeh Ting's troops joined the peasants of Hailufeng.
From that time on, it began to play the proper role of
the partisan troops and the Red Army. Another detachment
of the same army of Yeh Ting had also about one thousand
men. It was led by Chu Te and is now moving about the
border of Kwantung, Hunan and Kiangsi. It was joined by
the peasant detachment in those localities and forms a
large partisan army, assisting the peasants in the agrarian
revolution in southern Hunan, and in establishing many
local Soviet powers in a large number of districts.
    Another detachment of the National Revolutionary
Army which came over to our side was the Officers
Training Corps in the Canton Uprising. This regiment has
about a thousand men. After the defeat of the Canton
Uprising it went to Hai Feng and joined the above-mention-
ed detachment.
    All these forces combined made up the central
cadre of the Red Army in Hailufeng. After the loss of

partisan troop organisations, spreading its power in
different directions and pushing on the tide of the
agrarian revolution. Up to now these troops still form
the most useful military organisations for carrying on the
peasant uprisings in the eastern part of Kwantung.

    起初，贺龙和叶挺的军队中约有15,000名士兵。我们还有运作良好的党的士兵骨干和身为党员的军官。还有参加起义的武装工人和农民。但是，虽然南昌起义的目标是土地革命的结果，但它实际上并未促进土地革命。在革命军从南昌向南进军汕头的50天里，我们经过的地区从未受到土地革命的触动。因此，这支军队不仅未能作为工农红军开展积极工作，甚至未能达到农民游击队的效果。
    这支部队只有在失败后才接受了正确的领导，当时叶挺部队残部的一千多人加入了海陆丰的农民。从那时起，它开始发挥游击队和红军的适当作用。叶挺同一支军队的另一支部队也约有一千人。它由朱德率领，目前在广东、湖南和江西边境活动。它与当地的农民支队汇合，组成了一支庞大的游击队，协助湘南农民进行土地革命，并在许多地区建立了大量的地方苏维埃政权。
    归顺我方的国民革命军的另一支部队是广州起义中的军官教导团。该团约有千人。广州起义失败后，它前往海丰并与上述部队汇合。

The greatest shortcoming of the village partisan
troops and the Red Army in the Soviet District is that
although these troops themselves were formed under the
leadership of the proletariat, yet the present leading
capacity of the cities is still weak, the organisation of
the workers and their fighting capacity are not yet
strong enough to lead the coordinated action of the
cities and the villages. Hence these troops are still
carrying on their struggle in the form of partisan war-
fare. Although they have established a number of local
Soviets, they have not yet stirred up a high wave of civil
war, shaken the regime of the reactionary bourgeoisie and
imperialism in China.
Formerly we thought only the Parties in the
Eastern countries have not paid sufficient attention to
the work in the armies. But after hearing the reports and
discussions at the Congress, we realise that even our
brother Parties in the Western countries fail to devote
enough time and energy to this important question. The
experiences of the uprisings in China teach us that if we
do not succeed in shaking the foundations of the
imperialist army, our anti-war work will be mostly wasted
and no successful results will be obtained.
There are two peculiarities in regard to the
Chinese army that tend to make our work in the Chinese
army much easier than in the armies of Western countries.
First, the compact organisation of the European and
American armies and the comparatively better treatment
afforded to the soldiers usually create great difficulties
for those who carry on revolutionary activities in the
army. But the situation is entirely different in China.
Although the Chinese armies are mostly composed of
slum-proletarians rather than proper workers, the
standard of living of the soldiers are even lower than
the poorest workers and peasants. According to the
report of the Chief of Staff Ho Ying-chin of the
Military Committee of the Nanking Government, there are
84 armies in China divided into 800 divisions, with a
total of 2,200,000 men. The annual military expense is
720,000,000 dollars (mex). The armies of Chang Hsieh
Liang and Yang Tsung-Hsin are not included in this report.
But the possible annual income is only 400,000,000
dollars (mex). On account of this enormous discrepancy
between the income and the expenses, most of the
militarists have no means of meeting their army expenses.
Thus the militarists are talking of cutting down the
army. But, while thus talking, they are still carefully
watching each other, preparing for possible conflicts.
Many militarists are, on the one hand, adopting
the policy of not paying the soldiers and even of taking
the money intended for the payment of the soldiers for
their own use, and on the other hand, still recruiting
more soldiers for the purpose of extending territory under
their control. The result of this is naturally in-
tensified warfare between the militarists, and the
consequent increasing of the burden and suffering of the
workers and the peasants, and also the life of the
soldiers becomes more inhuman and unbearable. In the
face of such contradictions, the life of the Chinese
soldiers has no chance of being bettered. Their hunger
and suffering are becoming more acute every day. The
economic decline of the whole country, the bankruptcy in
the villages, and the growing unemployment prevent the
soldiers from finding a living outside of their miserable
and dangerous occupation. Moreover, the deepening of the
agrarian revolution and the spread of the slogans
"Armed Uprising" and "Power to the Soviets" among the

以前我们认为只有东方国家的政党没有充分重视军队中的工作。但在听取了大会上的报告和讨论后，我们意识到，甚至我们西方国家的兄弟政党也没有在这个重要问题上投入足够的时间和精力。中国起义的经验教训告诉我们，如果我们不能成功动摇帝国主义军队的基础，我们的反战工作将大部分付诸东流，无法取得成功的结果。
关于中国军队，有两个特点使得我们在华军队中的工作比在西方国家军队中容易得多。首先，欧美军队严密的组织和对士兵相对较好的待遇，通常给在军队中开展革命活动的人造成巨大困难。但中国的情况完全不同。虽然中国军队主要由流氓无产者而非正规工人组成，但士兵的生活水平甚至比最贫穷的工人和农民还要低。根据南京政府军事委员会参谋长何应钦的报告，中国有84个军，分为800个师，总兵力为2,200,000人。年度军费为7.2亿（墨西哥）元。张学良和杨虎城的军队未包含在此报告中。但可能的年收入仅为4亿（墨西哥）元。由于收支之间存在巨大差额，大多数军阀无力支付军费。因此，军阀们嚷嚷着裁军。但是，他们在这样叫嚷的同时，仍在互相严密监视，为可能发生的冲突做准备。许多军阀一方面采取不发军饷的政策，甚至将原本用于发放军饷的钱款挪作私用，另一方面仍招募更多士兵，以扩大其控制的地盘。其结果自然是军阀之间的战争加剧，进而增加了工人和农民的负担与苦难，士兵的生活也变得更加不人道和难以忍受。面对这样的矛盾，中国士兵的生活没有改善的机会。他们的饥饿和痛苦日益加剧。全国经济的衰退、农村的破产以及日益严重的失业，使士兵无法在这份悲惨且危险的行当之外谋生。此外，土地革命的深入以及“武装起义”和“一切权力归苏维埃”口号在

the imperialist countries, work among them is much more
difficult than work in the conscript armies. But the
mercenary armies of the colonial countries are quite
different. Work among this kind of army is even easier
than work among the conscript army in the imperialist
countries. It is easier for the workers and peasants
to enter the colonial mercenary army and to carry on
revolutionary activity among them.
From the experience of our work in the armies,
we feel that on the one hand, our brother Parties in the
West should do their best to struggle against the in-
correct tendencies in the proletarian masses concerning
this question and on the other hand, they should in-
tensify their work in the armies. The main points in
this work are: a) To send systematically organised Party
members and proletarian groups into the army (this is
easier in countries where there are voluntary and
mercenary armies); we must especially enter the
strategical departments of the army; b) If we cannot
become soldiers, we should apply for canteen work or
odd jobs in the army which are particularly fit for
propaganda work; c) Party nuclei and soldiers committees
should be set up in the army; d) Much emphasis should
be placed on creating and developing similar organisa-
tions in the navy; e) Propaganda and agitation in the
army should be considered as continuous and everyday work;
f) Struggle concerning the daily life of the soldiers
should sometimes receive more attention than political
struggles, because this is the best means for the
soldiers to realise their own strength.
The slogan "For the People's Defensive Corps",
can only be put forward in colonial countries where class
differentiation has not yet developed and where the

5.
工农群众中的传播，对士兵产生了巨大影响。因此，军队内部的阶级分化正在迅速发展，可以肯定地认为，士兵转向革命一方是不可避免的事实。
其次，“和平主义”、“废除常备军和警察民主化”、“人民军队”、“诅咒红军”、“回归土地”、“拒绝射击”、“拒绝服役”以及“以罢工回应战争”等错误口号，在中国工人、农民和士兵中尚未流行。相反，中国工农群众清醒地认识到，如果不推翻中国的本土士绅、资产阶级和新军阀，就没有和平的希望。只有当工人和农民在接受军事训练并拥有严密组织后，歼灭敌人的武装力量——从所谓的国民革命军到乡村警察等——并通过罢工和武装起义建立红军：只有这样，我们才能希望获得最终胜利和最终和平。
广州起义失败后，许多广东工人自愿参军，在士兵中开展革命工作。许多地方的失业工人自愿前往农村领导农民起义。起义被反动军队镇压后的失败农民群众，自愿组织游击队，推动土地革命的发展。同时，这些农民运动也动摇了反动武装力量本身。士兵和乡村警察加入乡村游击队的情况并不罕见。
从帝国主义国家雇佣军的角度来看，在其中开展工作比在征兵制军队中困难得多。但殖民地国家的雇佣军则完全不同。在这种军队中开展工作甚至比在帝国主义国家的征兵制军队中更容易。工人和农民更容易进入殖民地雇佣军并在其中开展革命活动。
根据我们在军队中工作的经验，我们认为，一方面，我们西方的兄弟政党应尽最大努力反对无产阶级群众在这一问题上的错误倾向，另一方面，他们应加强在军队中的工作。这项工作的主要要点是：a) 系统地将有组织的党员和无产阶级团体派入军队（在实行志愿兵制和雇佣兵制的国家这更容易）；我们必须特别进入军队的战略部门；b) 如果我们不能成为士兵，我们应该申请在军队中从事食堂工作或杂务，这些工作特别适合进行宣传；c) 应在军队中建立党团核心和士兵委员会；d) 应高度重视在海军中建立和发展类似组织；e) 军队中的宣传和鼓动应被视为持续性的日常工作；f) 有时应比政治斗争更关注涉及士兵日常生活的斗争，因为这是让士兵认识到自身力量的最佳手段。
“建立人民保卫团”的口号，只能在社会阶级分化尚未发展且

6.
revolutionary movement has not yet reached the stage of the
democratic revolution. In countries where the revolution
has already developed to the democratic stage, the slogan
"For the people's Defensive Corps" would mean a support of
the bourgeoisie, and should be dropped. Instead, slogans
for the organisation of Red Guards and Peasant Defence Corps
should be put forward. In countries where the revolution has
has already passed from the democratic revolution to the
proletarian stage, the slogan "For the People's Defence Corp"
is even less applicable. Because in this period, when a
dictatorship of the workers and peasants is in existence, or
when the revolution is in a stage of transition to a
dictatorship of the proletariat, the kind of military force
that such government requires must be either the Red Workers
and Peasants Army or the Red Army grown from the workers
Red Guard and Peasants Defence Corps (or partisan troops).
The national revolutionary army of the Chinese
bourgeoisie and new militarists has completely turned into a
counter-revolutionary armed force. Our tactics towards it
should be the same as our tactics toward the imperialist
army. We must propagate defeatism among such armies, and in
the process of their defeat we should absorb the revolutionary
soldiers into our workers' and peasants' army. We cannot
expect to turn the National Revolutionary Army as a whole into
a revolutionary army.
In the thesis, we think we should make our fight
against the imperialist partition of China a separate item,
just as we did in the case of the imperialist manoeuvres
against the Soviet Union.
In the face of Japanese military intervention in
Shantung and Manchuria, the Nanking Government, on the one
hand, prohibited the anti-Japanese movement of the masses,
and, on the other hand, tries to stir up the United States of
America against Japan, or it is even making secret deals with
Japan. Not only the worker and peasant masses are dissatisfied
with this shameful attitude of the Nanking Government, but
even the petty-bourgeoisie is showing signs of dissatisfaction.
Thus the left wing of the Kuomintang and the "Third Party"
elements, both demand that the mass movement should be re-
instated under the leadership of the Kuomintang, so that they
can use the mass movement in their bargain with the Japanese
imperialists. At the same time, this manoeuvre tends to
pacify the revolutionary fervour of the masses. The policy
of the Chinese Communist Party is to participate actively in
all anti-Japanese movements whenever it is a mass movement.
The purpose of our participation is to unmask the Nanking
Government's real policy of capitulation to the imperialists
and to expose the treacherous manoeuvre of the "Third Party"
elements to cheat the masses by sham revolutionary
demands. We must demonstrate to the masses that, under the
reactionary government, the only way out for the masses is
to conduct their own struggle against the Japanese imperial-
lists. To expect the reactionary government to re-
instate mass movements is absolutely Utopian and hopeless.
We should link this propaganda up with the slogans for the
armed uprising of the peasants, workers and poor people for
the overthrow of the Kuomintang political power, for a
thorough anti-imperialist movement and for the establishment
of political power. In the Kuomintang armies we should
intensify our propaganda and organisation work, because the
Tsinan butchery and the anti-Japanese movement has also
stirred up the soldier masses of the Kuomintang armies.
We must prepare for the inevitable situation when the
war breaks out, and for Fascist form of oppression. First,
we must make our Party factory nuclei work half illegally
even at the present time, so as to prepare for turning them
into complete illegal organisations when the situation demands,
secondly we must establish secret illegal Party nuclei in the
army so as fundamentally to shake the foundations of the
imperialist army.

6.
革命运动尚未达到民主革命阶段的殖民地国家提出。在革命已发展到民主阶段的国家，“建立人民保卫团”的口号意味着支持资产阶级，应予放弃。取而代之的是，应提出组织赤卫队和农民自卫队的口号。在革命已从民主革命过渡到无产阶级阶段的国家，“建立人民保卫团”的口号更不适用。因为在这一时期，当工农民主专政已经存在，或者革命处于向无产阶级专政过渡的阶段时，这种政府所需的军事力量必须是工农红军，或是由工人赤卫队和农民自卫队（或游击队）成长起来的红军。
中国资产阶级和新军阀的国民革命军已完全转变为反革命武装力量。我们对它的策略应与对帝国主义军队的策略相同。我们必须在此类军队中宣传失败主义，并在其溃败过程中吸收革命士兵加入我们的工农军队。我们不能指望将整个国民革命军转变为一支革命军队。
在决议案中，我们认为应将反对帝国主义瓜分中国的斗争作为一个单独的项目，就像我们对待帝国主义针对苏联的阴谋那样。
面对日本在山东和满洲的军事干涉，南京政府一方面禁止群众的反日运动，另一方面试图挑起美国对抗日本，甚至与日本进行秘密交易。不仅工农群众对南京政府这种可耻的态度感到不满，甚至小资产阶级也表现出不满的迹象。因此，国民党左派和“第三党”分子都要求恢复在国民党领导下的群众运动，以便他们利用群众运动作为与日本帝国主义讨价还价的筹码。同时，这一阴谋倾向于平息群众的革命热情。中国共产党的政策是，只要是群众运动，就积极参与所有反日运动。我们参与的目的是揭露南京政府对帝国主义投降的真实政策，并暴露“第三党”分子以虚假的革命要求欺骗群众的奸诈阴谋。我们必须向群众表明，在反动政府统治下，群众唯一的出路是开展自己反对日本帝国主义的斗争。指望反动政府恢复群众运动绝对是乌托邦式的，毫无希望。我们应该将这一宣传与农民、工人和贫民武装起义以推翻国民党政权、开展彻底的反帝运动和建立政权的口号联系起来。在国民党军队中，我们应该加强宣传和组织工作，因为济南惨案和反日运动也激起了国民党军队中广大士兵的情绪。
我们必须为战争爆发时不可避免的局面以及法西斯式的压迫做好准备。首先，即使目前也要使我们党的工厂核心工作处于半非法状态，以便在形势需要时将其转变为完全非法的组织；其次，我们必须在军队中建立秘密的非法党团核心，以便从根本上动摇帝国主义军队的基础。

POST OFFICE, SHANGHAI

Rules governing renting of Private Letter Boxes

1. Locked private boxes, into which all letters and postal packets other than insured letters and parcels will be sorted to be fetched by the addressee himself, may be rented at Post Office. The rent of the box assigned is to be paid half yearly or yearly in advance, and the box shall be closed if the rent for any period remains unpaid on the first day thereof. The rate of rent and the dimensions of the boxes may be obtained on inquiry at the District Accountancy.

2. Every person who desires to rent a private box shall, in addition to any other fee payable, deposit a sum of $5.00 as a guarantee for the return, in good order, of the keys of the box, which deposit shall be refunded on the keys being returned on the expiry of the tenancy of the box ; otherwise the deposit shall be forfeited to provide for the cost of fitting a new lock to enable the box to be re-let.

3. A key shall be supplied with each box, and additional keys, if required, may be obtained upon application in writing addressed to the Deputy Commissioner, District Accountancy, and on payment of a fee of 50 cents each, and must not be obtained elsewhere than from the Post Office. On a box-holder relinquishing the use of a box, he shall be required to return, at once, all keys supplied to him ; otherwise his deposit shall be retained as provided above.

4. If a box-holder who has rented a private box for a half-year or one year relinquishes the use of such box before the expiration of the period for which the fee has been paid, he shall, on return by him of all the keys of the box, be entitled to a refund of the fee paid for the period beyond the end of the quarter during which the box is relinquished.

5. If a key be lost, information must at once be given to the Post Office and the remaining key or keys (if any) returned. When a new lock, for which a charge shall be made, will be fitted in the box, and a key-and, if required, an additional key or keys-supplied.

6. A private box shall not be let to any person using a fictitious or assumed name.

7. The tenancy of a private box may be cancelled at any time if there is reason to believe that the box:-
(a) has been used by the tenant for or in connection with any illegal, fraudulent, indecent, or immoral purpose ; or
(b) is held, used, or controlled by a person who has been convicted of any offence involving fraud or dishonesty.
When the tenancy of a box is so cancelled, no portion of the fee paid for renting the box shall be refunded.

8. Private boxes shall be let only on the conditions prescribed in these regulations, and upon any breach thereof permission for the use of the box may be at once withdrawn.

9. Mail matter directed to a person or firm renting a private box, and mail matter directed to the number of a private box, will be deposited in the box, unless written notice is given to the contrary. Mail matter for persons addressed care of the holders of boxes can only be placed in private boxes when it is addressed to the number of the box.

10. As the sorting, and consequently the delivery, of correspondence will be materially facilitated when it bears as a part of the address, the number of the box, private box-holders are to be requested to have the number of their private box prominently shown on their letter paper, invoices, and other forms used by them in communicating with their correspondents, together with a request that, when addressing mail matter to them, the [number of the box] be included in the address.

上海邮局

私人信箱租赁规则

1. 除保价信函和包裹外，所有信件及邮政小包均会分拣至加锁的私人信箱中，由收件人自行提取，此类信箱可在邮局租赁。指定信箱的租金须每半年或每年预付，若在任何一期租期的首日租金仍未支付，则该信箱将被封闭。租金费率及信箱尺寸可向区会计科查询。

2. 凡欲租赁私人信箱者，除应付的其他费用外，须存入5.00美元作为保证金，以保证在租期届满时完好归还信箱钥匙；该保证金将在租期届满并归还钥匙时退还；否则，保证金将被没收，用于支付安装新锁的费用，以便将信箱重新出租。

3. 每个信箱配发一把钥匙，如需额外钥匙，可向区会计科副科长提交书面申请，并支付每把50美分的费用，且不得从邮局以外的地方获取钥匙。当信箱持有人放弃使用信箱时，须立即归还向其提供的所有钥匙；否则，其保证金将按上述规定予以保留。

4. 若已租赁私人信箱半年或一年的持有人在付费期限届满前放弃使用该信箱，在其归还该信箱所有钥匙后，有权获退超过放弃使用当季季度末之后期间的已付租金。

5. 若钥匙遗失，必须立即通知邮局，并归还剩余钥匙（如有）。随后将为信箱安装新锁（此项收费），并提供一把钥匙，以及根据需要提供的额外钥匙。

6. 私人信箱不得出租给使用虚构或化名的人士。

7. 若有理由相信信箱出现以下情况，可随时取消私人信箱的租赁：
(a) 租户将信箱用于或涉及任何非法、欺诈、淫秽或不道德的目的；或
(b) 信箱由曾因涉及欺诈或不诚实罪行而被定罪的人士持有、使用或控制。
当信箱租赁因此被取消时，已支付的任何部分租金均不予退还。

8. 私人信箱仅按本规章规定的条件出租，如有任何违反行为，使用信箱的许可可立即被撤销。

9. 寄给租赁私人信箱的个人或商号的邮件，以及寄往私人信箱号码的邮件，除非有书面通知相反要求，否则将投入该信箱。寄给由信箱持有人转交的人员的邮件，只有在其地址写明信箱号码时，方可放入私人信箱。

10. 由于在地址中包含信箱号码将大大便利信件的分拣及随后的投递，故要求私人信箱持有人在他们的信纸、发票及其他用于与通信对象联络的文件上，显著标明其私人信箱号码，并请求对方在向其寄送邮件时，将[信箱号码]列入地址。

The following is the new programme of the Chinese Communist
Party as drawn up by the Third International. Extract from
Inprekorr No. 64 dated September 19, 1928.

In the imperialist war for the oppression of the
colonies, the main tasks of the international proletariat
are, a) to propagate in the imperialist armies a defeatist
attitude; b) to organise national minority armies and lead
them in a revolutionary manner; c) to propagate fraterni-
sation between the soldiers in the imperialist armies and
the soldiers in the revolutionary armies in the colonies;
d) to turn the war for the suppression of the colonies into
civil war; e) to fight against such slogans as the defence
of the fatherland, the protection of citizens abroad, and
the solution of the problem of over-population; f) to oppose
the sending of gun-boats and the transportation of imperialist
troops to the colonies, the increasing of the war budget
and the extension of the term of military service, etc; g)
to send capable party members to the imperialist armies and
navies in the colonies to do organisation and propaganda
work, and to send comrades to brother parties in the
colonies to help them to do anti-imperialist work in the
armies. This work must be connected with the national revolu-
tionary movements in the colonies; h) if there are troops
recruited from colonial peoples in the imperialist army such
as Indians, Annamites African Negroes, Party members from such
colonial countries should be appointed to work among such troops;
i) work among the sailors in the navy should be intensified
by the different parties. This work will not only help the
proletarian revolution in the imperialist countries, but it
will be of great importance to the fight against war directed
against the Soviet Union and suppression of colonial revolu-
tion; j) to oppose the supply of ammunition, technicians, and
advisers to the counter-revolutionary armies in the colonies;
k) to oppose the imperialist intervention in the civil wars
in the colonies and the granting of loans by the imperialists
to the counter-revolutionary governments and militarists in
the colonies; l) to fight against the imperialist military
preparations in the concessions, railroads, and on the rivers
in the colonies; m) to oppose the imperialist butchery in the
colonies and all the measures which the imperialists adopt for
helping the native counter-revolutionary governments to
suppress the masses.

In the war among the imperialists for the ex-
ploitation of the colonies, the following methods in addition
to the above-mentioned must be used: a) to turn the war among
the imperialists for the exploitation of the colonies into a
civil war, and to work for the defeat of all the imperialist
powers engaged in the war; b) to oppose the assistance of the
native militarist groups engaged in a war among themselves by
the imperialists; c) to oppose all imperialist militarist pre-
parations in the colonies before the breaking out of the war.
Apart from this, application can be made of the general tasks
both before and after the breaking out of imperialist wars.

在帝国主义压迫殖民地的战争中，国际无产阶级的主要任务是：a) 在帝国主义军队中宣传失败主义态度；b) 组织少数民族军队并以革命方式领导他们；c) 宣传帝国主义军队中的士兵与殖民地革命军队中的士兵之间的 fraternisation（联欢/兄弟情谊）；d) 将镇压殖民地的战争转变为内战；e) 反对诸如保卫祖国、保护海外公民以及解决人口过剩问题等口号；f) 反对向殖民地派遣炮舰和运输帝国主义军队、增加战争预算以及延长服役期限等；g) 派遣能干的党员前往殖民地的帝国主义陆军和海军中进行组织和宣传工作，并派遣同志前往殖民地的兄弟党派，帮助他们在军队中开展反帝工作。这项工作必须与殖民地的民族革命运动相结合；h) 如果帝国主义军队中有从殖民地人民中招募的部队，如印度人、安南人（越南人）、非洲黑人，则应任命来自这些殖民国家的党员在这些部队中开展工作；i) 各党派应加强在海员中的工作。这项工作不仅有助于帝国主义国家的无产阶级革命，而且对于反对针对苏联的战争和镇压殖民地革命的斗争具有重要意义；j) 反对向殖民地的反革命军队提供弹药、技术人员和顾问；k) 反对帝国主义干涉殖民地的内战，以及帝国主义向殖民地的反革命政府和军阀提供贷款；l) 反对帝国主义在殖民地的租界、铁路和河流上的军事准备；m) 反对帝国主义在殖民地的屠杀行为，以及帝国主义为帮助当地反革命政府镇压民众而采取的一切措施。

在帝国主义列强争夺剥削殖民地的战争中，除上述方法外，还必须采用以下方法：a) 将帝国主义列强争夺剥削殖民地的战争转变为内战，并致力于使所有参战的帝国主义强国战败；b) 反对帝国主义援助相互交战的本国军阀集团；c) 在战争爆发前，反对殖民地里一切帝国主义的军事准备。除此之外，在帝国主义战争爆发前后，均可适用一般性任务。

关于内战准备工作，应在提纲中提出的四点基础上增加一个新点。在殖民地国家和拥有雇佣军的国家中，军事组织和训练在无产阶级群众中占据着异常重要的地位。虽然无产阶级在帝国主义国家已经学到了许多军事技术，但镇压起义的军事技术也在迅速改进。关于我们在起义期间的战术，也应增加一个新点。在

the one hand we have resolutely pointed out that as soon as the
insurrection is started, we must firmly go forward with all our
forces until our enemy is destroyed. On the other land, we must
point out that as soon as various symptoms of defeat have become
visible, we should quickly and determinedly adopt a policy of
retreat, in order to preserve the masses who participated in the
insurrection and our weapons, to enable us to prepare for another
attempt. During the July Insurrection in 1917, this, manoeuvre
was very skilfully executed. But after the defeat of the Canton
Insurrection, although a part of our military forces had safely
retreated to the villages to lead the peasant struggles, yet a
part of our forces was sacrificed on account of the lack of a plan
for a systematic retreat. The Shanghai Uprising also suffered
from similar mistake.
The Chinese Revolution is a very good example of
national marxist wars. During the Chinese Revolution in 1925-27
the Chinese Communist Party led the Chinese proletariat to take
part in the war for the unification of Kwantung and the Northern
Expedition, both of which were carried out under the leadership
of the Chinese bourgeoisie. During both wars, the Chinese Communist
Party made many opportunist errors, in the struggles against the
Rightward movement of the bourgeoisie and the struggle for leader-
ship of the revolution. These opportunist mistakes also affected
our attitude towards the national wars. This is because although
formally the war of unification of Kwantung and the Northern
Expedition are Anti-militarist struggle in fact, objectively, they
are primarily struggles which are bound to shake the foundation
of imperialist rule in China. Thus with the support and assistance
of the workers in the Hongkong Strike, the war for the unification
of Kwangtung succeeded in dealing a severe blow to the British
imperialists and forced them to carry out the 25% surtax proposal.
With the support of the Wuhan workers and the active participation
of the peasants of Hunan and Hupeh, the Northern Expedition
succeeded in taking back the British Concessions in Hankow and Kiukiang.
Because this civil war was revolutionary, was led
by the proletariat, and participated in by the peasants, the object-
ive task of the Chinese Communist Party should have been to establish
our own class army, to extend the workers and peasant military
organisations and training so as to assist the proletariat in its
struggle for the hegemony in the revolution. But the Chinese
Communist Party had practically overlooked all these points.
Although the objective conditions during the Northern Expedition
were fairly good, yet the Party failed to utilise the political
and military apparatus to carry out our own work in the army. And
further, the Party never tried to create our own military force.
Our Party had never realised that the mercenary character of the
National Revolutionary Army was a source of danger and that the
whole army could be easily turned into the tool of the militarists.
Our Party were chiefly engaged in political
manoeuvres among the upper layer of the officers, and considered
the making of alliances between generals the centre of our work.
The Party failed to take as the centre of our work the organisation
and propaganda among the lower strata of the soldier masses and
the changing of the character of the army by introducing worker
and peasant masses into the army. The Party did not sufficiently
realise the revolutionary meaning of the arming of the workers
and the peasants and their military training. The Party also had
failed to pay attention to the training of comrades for leading
military work. The Party had also failed to prepare for and lead
the partisan warfare of the peasants, to take in hand the organisation of
the scattered and therefore unsuccessful isolated peasant uprisings.

一方面，我们坚决指出，一旦起义开始，我们必须全力以赴，坚定推进，直至消灭敌人。另一方面，我们必须指出，一旦各种失败的迹象显现，我们就应迅速而果断地采取撤退政策，以保存参与起义的群众和我们的武器，使我们能够为下一次尝试做好准备。在1917年的七月起义中，这一机动策略执行得非常巧妙。但在广州起义失败后，虽然我军部分部队安全撤退到农村领导农民斗争，但由于缺乏系统撤退的计划，另一部分部队遭受了牺牲。上海起义也犯了类似的错误。
中国革命是民族马克思主义战争的一个很好的例子。在1925-27年的中国革命期间，中国共产党领导中国无产阶级参加了统一广东的战争和北伐战争，这两场战争都是在中国资产阶级的领导下进行的。在这两次战争中，中国共产党在反对资产阶级右倾运动和争取革命领导权的斗争中，犯了许多机会主义错误。这些机会主义错误也影响了我们对民族战争的态度。这是因为，虽然形式上统一广东的战争和北伐战争是反军阀斗争，但实际上，客观上，它们主要是必然动摇帝国主义在华统治基础的斗争。因此，在香港罢工工人的支持和协助下，统一广东的战争成功给予英国帝国主义者沉重打击，迫使他们实施25%附加税提案。在武汉工人的支持和湖南、湖北农民的积极参与下，北伐军成功收回了汉口和九江的英国租界。
因为这场内战是革命性的，由无产阶级领导，并有农民参与，中国共产党的客观任务本应是建立我们自己的阶级军队，扩大工农军事组织和训练，以协助无产阶级争取革命领导权的斗争。但中国共产党实际上忽视了所有这些要点。虽然北伐期间的客观条件相当有利，但党未能利用政治和军事机构在军队中开展我们的工作。此外，党从未试图创建我们自己的军事力量。我们党从未认识到国民革命军的雇佣兵性质是一个危险源，整个军队很容易沦为军阀的工具。
我们党主要致力于在军官上层进行政治 maneuvering（权术操作），并将将军之间的结盟视为我们工作的中心。党未能将士兵群众下层的组织和宣传，以及通过引入工农群众来改变军队性质作为我们工作的中心。党没有充分认识到武装工人和农民及其军事训练的革命意义。党也未能注意培养领导军事工作的同志。党也未能准备和领导农民的游击战，未能着手组织那些分散因而失败的孤立农民起义。

These mistakes can be considered as the chief
of the military defeat of the proletariat in the Northei.
Expedition. Thus, when Wuhan followed Nanking and walked ...co
the counter-revolutionary camp, our Party could only use the
armies of Yeh Ting and Ho Lung to make a heroic protest (the
Nanchang Uprising) at the moment of defeat, and was not able
to go a step forward and convert this protest into civil war
for the overthrow of the political power of the bourgeoisie,
the militarists and the gentry.
At the beginning we had about 15,000 soldiers in the
armies of Ho Lung and Yeh Ting. We had also soldiers' nuclei
of the Party functioning fairly well and officers who are Party
members. There were also armed workers and peasants who parti-
cipated in the uprising. But although the aim of the Nanchang
Uprising was the outcome of the agrarian revolution, yet it has
done practically nothing to promote the agrarian revolution.
During the 50 days southward march of the revolutionary army
from Nanchang to Swatow, the regions through which we marched
were never touched by the agrarian revolution. Thus this army
not only failed to do positive work as a Workers and Peasants
Army, but it even failed to achieve the results of a peasant
partisan troop.
The army received correct leadership only after its
defeat, when about over a thousand men of the remnants of
Yeh Ting's troops joined the peasants of Hailufeng. From that
time on, it began to play the proper role of the partisan troops
and the Red Army. Another detachment of the same army of Yeh Ting
had also about one thousand men. It was led by Chu Te and is now
moving about the border of Kwantung, Hunan and Kiangsi. It was
joined by the peasant detachment in those localities and forms a
large partisan army, assisting the peasants in the agrarian
revolution in southern Hunan, and in establishing many local
Soviet powers in a large number of districts.
Another detachment of the National Revolutionary Army
which came over to our side was the Officers Training Corps in
the Canton Uprising. This regiment has about a thousand men.
After the defeat of the Canton Uprising it went to Hai Feng
and joined the above-mentioned detachment.
All these forces combined made up the central cadre
of the Red Army in Hailufeng. After the loss of the cities
of Hailufeng, the Red Army was divided into partisan troop organisat-
ions, spreading its power in different directions and pushing
on the tide of the agrarian revolution. Up to now these troops
still form the most useful military organisations for carrying
on the peasant uprisings in the eastern part of Kwantung.
Apart from the above mentioned comparatively large
armed revolutionary bodies, there are many partisan troops in
the Yangtse Kiang and Chu Kiang valleys which came to our side
from the Kuomintang armies. These troops are spread over the
Kwantung, Hunan, Kiangsi, Hupeh and Honan provinces and are
assisting the peasant masses of these provinces in the agrarian
revolution. There is another kind of the peasant armed forces
which is formed by the peasants arming themselves with guns and
other military weapons seized from the reactionary armies by
the peasants. The most successful case of this kind is in the
Hainan Island. There are about a thousand men, with a very good
Party leadership and more centralised Red Army organisation.
In many Chinese villages, the cases of the peasants attempting
to seize the arms of the regular troops with only one or two
rifles or with simply primitive weapons are not infrequent.

起初，贺龙和叶挺的军队中约有15,000名士兵。我们还有运作良好的党的士兵核心以及身为党员的军官。还有参与起义的武装工人和农民。但是，虽然南昌起义的目标是土地革命的结果，但它实际上并未促进土地革命。在革命军从南昌到汕头南下的50天行军中，我们经过的地区从未受到土地革命的触动。因此，这支军队不仅未能作为工农红军开展积极工作，甚至未能取得农民游击队的成果。
这支部队只有在失败后才接受了正确的领导，当时叶挺部队的残部约一千余人加入了海陆丰的农民。从那时起，它开始发挥游击队和红军的适当作用。叶挺同一支军队的另一分队也约有千人。由朱德率领，目前在广东、湖南和江西边境活动。它与当地的农民分队汇合，组成了一支庞大的游击队，协助湘南农民进行土地革命，并在许多地区建立了众多地方苏维埃政权。
倒戈加入我方的一支国民革命军部队是广州起义中的军官教导团。该团约有千人。广州起义失败后，它前往海丰并加入了上述分队。
所有这些力量联合起来，构成了海陆丰红军的核心骨干。在海陆丰城市失守后，红军被划分为游击队组织，向不同方向扩展其影响力，推动土地革命的浪潮。到目前为止，这些部队仍然是广东东部开展农民起义最有用的军事组织。
除了上述规模较大的武装革命团体外，在长江和珠江流域还有许多从国民党军队中投奔我方的游击队。这些部队分布在广东、湖南、江西、湖北和河南各省，正在协助这些省的农民群众进行土地革命。还有一种农民武装力量，是由农民用从反动军队手中缴获的枪支和其他军事武器武装自己而形成的。这方面最成功的案例是在海南岛。那里约有千人，拥有非常好的党的领导以及更集中的红军组织。在中国许多村庄，农民仅凭一两支步枪或仅用原始武器试图夺取正规军武器的情况并不少见。

The greatest shortcoming of the village partisan
troops and the Red Army in the Soviet District is that although
these troops themselves were formed under the leadership of the
proletariat, yet the present leading capacity of the cities
is still weak, the organisation of the workers and their fighting
capacity are not yet strong enough to lead the co-ordinated
action of the cities and the villages. Hence these troops are
still carrying on their struggle in the form of partisan
warfare. Although they have established a number of local
Soviets, they have not yet stirred up a high wave of civil
war, shaken the regime of the reactionary bourgeoisie and
imperialism in China.
Formerly we thought only the Parties in the Eastern
countries have not paid sufficient attention to the work in the
armies. But after hearing the reports and discussions at the
Congress, we realise that even our brother Parties in the
Western countries fail to devote enough time and energy to this
important question. The experience of the uprisings in China
teach us that if we do not succeed in shaking the foundations
of the imperialist army, our anti-war work will be mostly wasted
and no successful results will be obtained.
There are two peculiarities in regard to the Chinese
Army that tend to make our work in the Chinese army much easier
than in the armies of Western countries. First, the compact
organisation of the European and American armies and the
comparatively better treatment afforded to the soldiers usually
create great difficulties for those who carry on revolutionary
activities in the army. But the situation is entirely different
in China. Although the Chinese armies are mostly composed of
slum-proletarians rather than proper workers, the standard of
living of the soldiers are even lower than the poorest workers
and peasants. According to the report of the Chief of Staff
Ho Ying Chin of the Military Committee of the Nanking Government,
there are 84 armies in China divided into 800 divisions, with a
total of 2,200,000 men. The annual military expense is
720,000,000 dollars (mex). The armies of Chang Hsieh Liang and
Yang Tsung-Hsin are not included in this report. But the
possible income is only 400,000,000 dollars (mex). On account
of this enormous discrepancy between the income and the expenses,
most of the militarists have no means of meeting their army
expenses. Thus the militarists are talking of cutting down the
army. But, while thus talking, they are still carefully watching
each other, preparing for possible conflicts.
Many militarists are, on the one hand, adopting the
policy of not paying the soldiers and even of taking the money
intended for the payment of the soldiers for their own use, and
on the other hand, still recruiting more soldiers for the purpose
of extending territory under their control. The result of this is
naturally intensified warfare between the militarists, and the
subsequent increasing of the burden and suffering of the workers
and the peasants, and also the life of the soldiers becomes more
inhuman and unbearable. In the face of such contradictions, the
life of the Chinese soldiers has no chance of being bettered.
Their hunger and suffering are becoming more acute every day.
The economic decline of the whole country, the bankruptcy in the
villages, and the growing unemployment prevent the soldiers
from finding a living outside of their miserable and dangerous
occupation. Moreover, the deepening of the agrarian revolution
and the spread of the slogans "Armed Uprising" and "Power to the
Soviets" among the worker and peasant masses are having a great
influence on the soldiers. Thus the process of the class
differentiation is developing rapidly in the army and it can be
safely considered as an inevitable fact that the soldiers will
come to the side of the revolution.

苏区乡村游击队和红军最大的缺点是，虽然这些部队本身是在无产阶级领导下组建的，但目前城市的领导能力仍然薄弱，工人的组织及其战斗力尚不足以领导城乡协调行动。因此，这些部队仍以游击战的形式进行斗争。虽然他们建立了一些地方苏维埃，但尚未掀起内战的高潮，动摇中国反动资产阶级和帝国主义的政权。
以前我们认为只有东方国家的政党没有充分重视军队中的工作。但在听取大会的报告和讨论后，我们意识到，即使是我们西方国家的兄弟政党，也没有在这个重要问题上投入足够的时间和精力。中国起义的经验告诉我们，如果我们不能成功动摇帝国主义军队的基础，我们的反战工作大部分将是徒劳的，不会取得成功的结果。
关于中国军队，有两个特点使得我们在华军队中的工作比在西方国家军队中容易得多。首先，欧美军队严密的组织和对士兵相对较好的待遇，通常给在军队中从事革命活动的人造成巨大困难。但中国的情况完全不同。虽然中国军队主要由流氓无产者而非正式工人组成，但士兵的生活水平甚至比最贫穷的工人和农民还要低。根据南京政府军事委员会参谋长何应钦的报告，中国有84个军，分为800个师，总人数为2,200,000人。年度军费开支为7.2亿墨西哥元。张学良和杨森（音译）的军队未包含在此报告中。但可能的收入仅为4亿墨西哥元。由于收支存在巨大差额，大多数军阀无力支付军费。因此，军阀们嚷嚷着裁军。但是，在这样叫嚷的同时，他们仍在互相严密监视，为可能发生的冲突做准备。
许多军阀一方面采取不发饷甚至挪用士兵军饷供自己使用的政策，另一方面仍招募更多士兵以扩大其控制领土。其结果自然是军阀间的战争加剧，随后增加了工人和农民的负担与苦难，士兵的生活也变得更加不人道和难以忍受。面对这样的矛盾，中国士兵的生活没有改善的机会。他们的饥饿和痛苦日益加剧。全国经济的衰退、农村的破产以及日益严重的失业，使士兵无法在他们悲惨且危险的职业之外谋生。此外，土地革命的深化以及“武装起义”和“苏维埃掌权”口号在工农群众中的传播，对士兵产生了巨大影响。因此，军队内部的阶级分化过程正在迅速发展，可以肯定地认为，士兵转向革命一方是不可避免的事实。

Secondly, such incorrect slogans as "Pacifism",
"abolition" of the standing army and the demonstration of
the police", "the people's army", "curse the red army",
"return to the land", "refuse to shoot", "refuse to serve",
and "to answer wars with strikes" are not yet prevalent among
the Chinese workers, peasants and soldiers. On the contrary,
the Chinese workers and peasant mass are consciously rea-
lising that without the overthrow of the Chinese native gentry,
bourgeoisie and new militarists, there is no hope for peace.
Only when the workers and peasants, after receiving military
training and having a compact organisation annihilate the
armed forces of our enemies, - from the so-called national
revolutionary army to the village police, etc - and, by means
of strikes and armed uprisings, create a Red Army: only then
can we hope for final victory and final peace.
After the defeat of the Canton Uprising, many
workers of Kwantung voluntarily entered the army to carry
on revolutionary work among the soldiers. The unemployed
workers of many places voluntarily went to the village to
lead the peasant uprisings. The defeated peasant masses
whose uprising was crushed by the reactionary troops were
going voluntarily to organise partisan troops which push
forward the development of the agrarian revolution. At the
same time, these movements of the peasants shook the react-
ionary armed forces themselves. It is not unusual that
soldiers and village police come to join the village partisan
troops.
From the point of view of mercenary armies of the
imperialist countries, work among them is much more difficult
than work in the conscript armies. But the mercenary armies
of the colonial countries are quite different. Work among
this kind of army is even easier than work among the cons-
cript army in the imperialist countries. It is easier for
the workers and peasants to enter the colonial mercenary
army and to carry on revolutionary activity among them.
From the experience of our work in the armies,
we feel that on the one hand, our brother Parties in the
West should do their best to struggle against the incorrect
tendencies in the proletarian masses concerning this
question and on the other hand, they should intensify their
work in the armies. The main points in this work are: a)
To send systematically organised Party members and prole-
tarian groups into the army (this is easier in countries
where there are voluntary and mercenary armies): we must
especially enter the strategical departments of the army;
b) If we cannot become soldiers, we should apply for
canteen work or odd jobs in the army which are particularly
fit for propaganda work; c) Party nuclei and soldiers
committees should be set up in the army; d) Much emphasis
should be placed on creating and developing similar organi-
sations in the navy; e) Propaganda and agitation in the army
should be considered as continuous and everyday work; f)
Struggle concerning the daily life of the soldiers should
sometimes receive more attention than political struggles,
because this is the best means for the soldiers to realise
their own strength.
The slogans "For the People's Defensive Corps"
can only be put forward in colonial countries where class
differentiation has not yet developed and where the revolu-
tionary movement has not yet reached the stage of the
democratic revolution. In countries where the revolution
has already developed to the democratic stage, the slogan
"For the people's Defensive Corps" would mean a support of
the bourgeoisie, and should be dropped. Instead, slogans

其次，诸如“和平主义”、“废除常备军和警察示威”、“人民军队”、“诅咒红军”、“回到土地上去”、“拒绝射击”、“拒绝服役”以及“以罢工回应战争”等不正确的口号，在中国工人、农民和士兵中尚未流行。相反，中国工农群众正自觉地认识到，如果不推翻中国的本土士绅、资产阶级和新军阀，就没有和平的希望。只有当工人和农民在接受军事训练并拥有严密组织之后，歼灭从所谓的国民革命军到乡村警察等一切敌人的武装力量，并通过罢工和武装起义建立一支红军时，我们才有希望获得最终胜利和最终和平。

广州起义失败后，许多广东工人自愿参军，在士兵中开展革命工作。许多地方的失业工人自愿前往农村，领导农民起义。那些起义被反动军队镇压的失败农民群众，正自愿组织游击队，推动土地革命的发展。同时，这些农民运动也动摇了反动武装力量本身。士兵和乡村警察加入乡村游击队的情况并不罕见。

从帝国主义国家雇佣军的角度来看，在其中开展工作比在征召入伍的军队中开展工作要困难得多。但殖民地国家的雇佣军则完全不同。在这种军队中开展工作甚至比在帝国主义国家的征召入伍军队中开展工作更容易。工人和农民更容易进入殖民地雇佣军并在其中开展革命活动。

根据我们在军队中的工作经验，我们认为，一方面，我们在西方的兄弟党应尽力反对无产阶级群众在这一问题上的不正确倾向；另一方面，他们应加强在军队中的工作。这项工作的主要要点是：a) 系统地将有组织的党员和无产阶级团体派入军队（在实行志愿兵役制和雇佣兵制的国家这更容易）：我们必须特别打入军队的战略部门；b) 如果我们不能成为士兵，我们就应申请在军队中从事食堂工作或杂务，这些工作特别适合进行宣传；c) 应在军队中建立党的核心组织和士兵委员会；d) 应高度重视在海军中创建和发展类似组织；e) 军队中的宣传和鼓动工作应被视为持续性的日常工作；f) 有时应比政治斗争更关注有关士兵日常生活的斗争，因为这是让士兵认识到自身力量的最佳手段。

“为了人民防卫团”的口号只能在阶级分化尚未发展、革命运动尚未达到民主革命阶段的殖民地国家提出。在革命已发展到民主阶段的国家，“为了人民防卫团”的口号意味着支持资产阶级，因此应予放弃。取而代之的是，应提出

for the organisation of Red Guards and Peasant Defence Corps
should be put forward. In countries where the revolution
has already passed from the democratic revolution to the
proletarian stage, the slogan "For the People's Defence Corps",
is even less applicable. Because in this period, when a
dictatorship of the workers and peasants is in existence, or
when the revolution is in a stage of transition to a
dictatorship of the proletariat, the kind of military force
that such government requires must be either the Red Workers
and Peasants Army or the Red Army grown from the workers
Red Guard and Peasants Defence Corps (or partisan troops).
The national revolutionary army of the Chinese
bourgeoisie and new militarists has completely turned into a
counter-revolutionary armed force. Our tactics toward it
should be the same as our tactics toward the imperialist army.
We must propagate defeatism among such armies, and in the
process of their defeat we should absorb the revolutionary
soldiers into our workers' and peasants' army. We cannot
expect to turn the National Revolutionary Army as a whole into
a revolutionary army.
In the thesis, we think we should make our fight
against the imperialist partition of China a separate item,
just as we did in the case of the imperialist manoeuvres
against the Soviet Union.
In the face of Japanese military intervention in
Shantung and Manchuria, the Nanking Government, on the one
hand, prohibited the anti-Japanese movement of the masses,
and, on the other hand, tries to stir up the United States of
America against Japan, or if it even making secret deals with
Japan. Not only the worker and peasant masses are dissatisfied
with this shameful attitude of the Nanking Government, but
even the petty-bourgeoisie is showing signs of dissatisfaction.
Thus the Left Wing of the Kuomintang and the "Third Party"
elements, both demand that the mass movement should be re-
instated under the leadership of the Kuomintang, so that they
can use the mass movement in their bargain with the Japanese
imperialists. At the same time, this manoeuvre tends to
pacify the revolutionary fervour of the masses. The policy
of the Chinese Communist Party is to participate actively in
all anti-Japanese movements whenever it is a mass movement.
The purpose of our participation is to unmask the Nanking
Government's real policy of capitulation to the imperialists
and to expose the treacherous manoeuvre of the "Third Party"
elements to cheat the masses by sham revolutionary demands.
We must demonstrate to the masses that, under the reactionary
government, the only way out for the masses is to conduct
their own struggle against the Japanese imperialists. To
expect the reactionary government to reinstate mass movements
is absolutely Utopian and hopeless. We should link this
propaganda up with the slogans for the armed uprising of the
peasants, workers and poor people for the overthrow of the
Kuomintang political power, for a thorough anti-imperialist
movement and for the establishment of political power. In the
Kuomintang armies we should intensify our propaganda and
organisation work, because the Tsinan butchery and the anti-
Japanese movement has also stirred up the soldier masses of
the Kuomintang armies.
We must prepare for the inevitable situation when
the war breaks out, and for Fascist form of oppression. First,
we must make our Party factory nuclei work half illegally even
at the present time, so as to prepare for turning them into
complete illegal organisations when the situation demands.
Secondly we must establish secret illegal party nuclei in the
army so as fundamentally to shake the foundations of the
imperialist army.

组织赤卫队和农民自卫队的口号。在革命已从民主革命过渡到无产阶级阶段的国家，“为了人民防卫团”的口号更不适用。因为在这一时期，当工农民主专政已经存在，或者革命处于向无产阶级专政过渡的阶段时，这种政府所需的军事力量必须是工农红军，或是由工人赤卫队和农民自卫队（或游击队）发展而来的红军。

中国资产阶级和新军阀的国民革命军已完全转变为反革命武装力量。我们对它的策略应与对帝国主义军队的策略相同。我们必须在这类军队中宣传失败主义，并在其溃败过程中吸收革命士兵加入我们的工农军队。我们不能指望将整个国民革命军转变为一支革命军队。

在提纲中，我们认为应将反对帝国主义瓜分中国的斗争作为一个单独的项目列出，就像我们在处理帝国主义针对苏联的阴谋时所做的那样。

面对日本在山东和满洲的军事干涉，南京政府一方面禁止群众的反日运动，另一方面试图挑起美国对抗日本，甚至与日本进行秘密交易。不仅工农群众对南京政府这种可耻的态度感到不满，甚至小资产阶级也表现出不满的迹象。因此，国民党左派和“第三党”分子都要求在国民党领导下恢复群众运动，以便他们利用群众运动作为与日本帝国主义讨价还价的筹码。同时，这一伎俩倾向于平息群众的革命热情。中国共产党的政策是，只要是群众运动，就积极参与所有反日运动。我们参与的目的是揭露南京政府对帝国主义投降的真实政策，并暴露“第三党”分子以虚假的革命要求欺骗群众的背叛行径。我们必须向群众表明，在反动政府统治下，群众唯一的出路是开展自己反对日本帝国主义的斗争。指望反动政府恢复群众运动是绝对乌托邦式且没有希望的。我们应该将这一宣传与农民、工人和贫民武装起义以推翻国民党政权、开展彻底的反帝运动和建立政权的口号联系起来。在国民党军队中，我们应加强宣传和组织工作，因为济南惨案和反日运动也激起了国民党军队中广大士兵的情绪。

我们必须为战争爆发时的不可避免局势以及法西斯式的压迫做好准备。首先，即使目前，我们也必须使党的工厂核心组织处于半非法状态，以便在形势需要时将其转变为完全非法的组织。其次，我们必须在军队中建立秘密的非法党的核心组织，从而从根本上动摇帝国主义军队的基础。

The following is the new programme of the Chinese Communist
Party as drawn up by the Third International. Extract from
Inprekorr No. 64 dated September 19, 1928.

In the imperialist war for the oppression of the
colonies, the main tasks of the international proletariat
are, a) to propagate in the imperialist armies a defeatist
attitude; b) to organise national minority armies and lead
them in a revolutionary manner; c) to propagate fraterni-
sation between the soldiers in the imperialist armies and
the soldiers in the revolutionary armies in the colonies;
d) to turn the war for the suppression of the colonies into
civil war; e) to fight against such slogans as the defence
of the fatherland, the protection of citizens abroad, and
the solution of the problem of over-population; f) to oppose
the sending of gun-boats and the transportation of imperialist
troops to the colonies, the increasing of the war budget
and the extension of the term of military service, etc; g)
to send capable party members to the imperialist armies and
navies in the colonies to do organisation and propaganda
work, and to send comrades to brother parties in the
colonies to help them to do anti-imperialist work in the
armies. This work must be connected with the national revolu-
tionary movements in the colonies; h) if there are troops
recruited from colonial peoples in the imperialist army such
as Indians, Annamites African Negroes, Party members from such
colonial countries should be appointed to work among such troops;
i) work among the sailors in the navy should be intensified
by the different parties. This work will not only help the
proletarian revolution in the imperialist countries, but it
will be of great importance to the fight against war directed
against the Soviet Union and suppression of colonial revolu-
tion; j) to oppose the supply of ammunition, technicians, and
advisers to the counter-revolutionary armies in the colonies;
k) to oppose the imperialist intervention in the civil wars
in the colonies and the granting of loans by the imperialists
to the counter-revolutionary governments and militarists in
the colonies; l) to fight against the imperialist military
preparations in the concessions, railroads, and on the rivers
in the colonies; m) to oppose the imperialist butchery in the
colonies and all the measures which the imperialists adopt for
helping the native counter-revolutionary governments to
suppress the masses.

In the war among the imperialists for the ex-
ploitation of the colonies, the following methods in addition
to the above-mentioned must be used: a) to turn the war among
the imperialists for the exploitation of the colonies into a
civil war, and to work for the defeat of all the imperialist
powers engaged in the war; b) to oppose the assistance of the
native militarist groups engaged in a war among themselves by
the imperialists; c) to oppose all imperialist militarist pre-
parations in the colonies before the breaking out of the war.
Apart from this, application can be made of the general tasks
both before and after the breaking out of imperialist wars.

In regard to the preparations for civil war, a
new point should be added to the four points suggested in the
theses. Military organisation and training occupies an except-
ionally important place in the proletarian masses in the colonial
countries and countries with a mercenary army. Although the
proletariat has learned a lot of military technique in the
imperialist countries, yet the military technique of combating
uprisings is quickly improving. Regarding our tactics during
the insurrection, a new point should also be added. On

在帝国主义压迫殖民地的战争中，国际无产阶级的主要任务是：a) 在帝国主义军队中宣传失败主义态度；b) 组织少数民族军队并以革命方式领导它们；c) 宣传帝国主义军队中的士兵与殖民地革命军队中的士兵之间的 fraternisation（联欢/友好关系）；d) 将镇压殖民地的战争转变为内战；e) 反对保卫祖国、保护海外公民以及解决人口过剩问题等口号；f) 反对向殖民地派遣炮舰和运输帝国主义军队、增加战争预算和延长服役期限等；g) 派遣能干的党员到殖民地的帝国主义陆军和海军中进行组织和宣传工作，并派遣同志到殖民地的兄弟党那里，帮助他们在军队中进行反帝工作。这项工作必须与殖民地的民族革命运动相结合；h) 如果帝国主义军队中有从殖民地人民中招募的部队，如印度人、安南人（越南人）、非洲黑人，则应任命来自这些殖民国家的党员在这些部队中工作；i) 各党应加强在海军水手中间的工作。这项工作不仅有助于帝国主义国家的无产阶级革命，而且对于反对针对苏联的战争和镇压殖民地革命的斗争具有重要意义；j) 反对向殖民地的反革命军队提供弹药、技术人员和顾问；k) 反对帝国主义干涉殖民地的内战，以及帝国主义向殖民地的反革命政府和军阀提供贷款；l) 反对帝国主义在殖民地的租界、铁路和河流上的军事准备；m) 反对帝国主义在殖民地的屠杀行为，以及帝国主义为帮助本土反革命政府镇压群众而采取的一切措施。

在帝国主义列强为剥削殖民地而进行的战争中，除上述方法外，还必须采用以下方法：a) 将帝国主义列强为剥削殖民地而进行的战争转变为内战，并致力于使所有参战的帝国主义强国遭受失败；b) 反对帝国主义援助彼此交战的本土军阀集团；c) 在战争爆发前，反对殖民地里一切帝国主义的军事准备。除此之外，在帝国主义战争爆发前后，均可适用一般性任务。

mined to drive out from China the British, Japanese, American 
and French imperialists, and to overthrow the Kuomintang and 

the Nanking Government, the running dogs of the imperialists 

and the traitors to the Chinese revolution. Thus notwithstanding 
the raging white terror of the Kuomintang, the systematic and 
most ruthless mass executions and massacres of revolutionary 
workers and peasants, strikes and political mass demonstrations 
of ever-increasing dimensions are frequently taking place.
